proof.text: Write $i:\mathcal A_S\hookrightarrow\mathcal A$ for the full inclusion. By [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints], $\mathcal A_S$ is presentable, its reflector is left adjoint to $i$, and its small colimits are obtained by reflecting the corresponding ambient colimits. Both categories are presentable and $L$ has a right adjoint, so the same node's adjoint criterion says that $L$ preserves all small colimits. Put $W=\langle S\rangle$, the class in [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation]. That statement identifies $W$ with the arrows inverted by $L$, and puts every unit $\eta_A:A\to iLA$ in $W$. The adjunction is the one in the question; the small-set reflector and its adjunction may be identified with it by their mapping-space universal property.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.20, setup; Proposition 5.5.4.15 for the inverted class; read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: The counit $\epsilon:Li\to\mathrm{id}$ is an equivalence. To check this directly, for $B,Z\in\mathcal A_S$ fullness and the mapping-space adjunction in [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] give $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_S}(B,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(iB,iZ)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_S}(LiB,Z)$. This equivalence is precomposition with $\epsilon_B$: the triangle identity $i\epsilon_B\,\eta_{iB}\simeq1_{iB}$ identifies its adjunction transpose with $i$ of the given map. Yoneda full faithfulness for the opposite category from [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] detects that $\epsilon_B$ is an equivalence. The pointwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] then makes $\epsilon$ an equivalence of functors. This uses no presentability or adjoint-functor theorem for $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.20; elementary full-inclusion counit argument using Section 5.2.7; read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: Fix a cocontinuous $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E$ that inverts $S$, and put $T=\{f:F(f)\text{ is an equivalence}\}$. It contains $S$ and all equivalences and satisfies two-out-of-three, since functors preserve inverses and composition. It is retract closed: if $u:P\to Q$ is a retract of an invertible $v:P'\to Q'$ with sections $a,b$ and retractions $r,t$, its inverse is $rv^{-1}b$; the identities follow from $va=bu$, $ur=tv$, $ra=1$, $tb=1$ in the homotopy category. Apply this to $F$ of a retract diagram. Also $T$ is pushout closed. Indeed $F$ takes a pushout of $f$ to a pushout of $Ff$. Mapping this latter square into any $e\in\mathcal E$ gives a pullback square of spaces by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. When $Ff$ is invertible the resulting pullback projection is an equivalence (pull back its inverse). The same node's Yoneda full faithfulness, applied to the opposite category, detects that the pushed-out arrow is an equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.11 and Definition 5.5.4.5; elementary closure verification; read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: The class $T$ is closed under small colimits in the arrow infinity category. For a small diagram of arrows in $T$, [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] computes its colimit at its source and target. Cocontinuity of $F$ identifies the resulting arrow with the colimit of the transformed diagram of arrows in $\mathcal E$. This diagram is a transformation between its source and target diagrams with equivalence components, so it is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Applying the colimit functor to it and its inverse gives inverse arrows. Thus its colimit is an equivalence. Step 3 and this observation show that $T$ contains $S$ and has every closure property in the definition of $W$ in [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation]. Minimality gives $W\subseteq T$. In particular every $F\eta_A$ is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.4.11 and the last paragraph of Proposition 5.5.4.20; read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: Define $G=Fi$. Let $q:J\to\mathcal A_S$ be small and let $c=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal A}iq$ with cocone $\iota_j:iq_j\to c$. The colimit formula of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] gives the colimit cocone $\lambda_j=L\iota_j\,\epsilon_{q_j}^{-1}:q_j\to Lc$. The counit is invertible by Step 2, and the triangle identity gives $i\epsilon_{q_j}^{-1}\simeq\eta_{iq_j}$. Naturality of the unit therefore gives $i\lambda_j\simeq iL\iota_j\,\eta_{iq_j}\simeq\eta_c\,\iota_j$, coherently in $j$. Applying $F$, the map $F\eta_c:Fc\to FiLc$ is an equivalence by Step 4 and compares the cocones $F\iota$ and $Fi\lambda$ on the same diagram $Fiq$. For any $e\in\mathcal E$, precomposition with $F\eta_c$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}(FiLc,e)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(Fc,e)$. Since $F\iota$ is colimiting, the latter is $\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(Fiq_j,e)$. The coherent identity above says that this composite is exactly the map induced by $Fi\lambda$. The colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] therefore proves that $Fi\lambda$ is colimiting. This includes $J=\varnothing$ and proves that $Fi$ preserves all small colimit cocones.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.20; explicit check that the restriction to local objects is cocontinuous; read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: For a cocontinuous $G:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal E$, the composite $GL$ is cocontinuous because $L$ is, by Step 1. Every $s\in S$ lies in $W$, and the criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] makes $Ls$ an equivalence. Its image under $G$ is an equivalence. Thus precomposition with $L$ takes the left-hand full functor category into the right-hand full functor category. Step 5 shows that restriction along $i$ defines a functor in the other direction. Precomposition acts on coherent diagrams of functors by composition, so these are functors on the full categories, including their higher simplices.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.20; the forward direction; read online, not archived in literature/

proof.text: On the right-hand full category, whiskering the unit gives the natural transformation $F\mapsto F\eta:F\to FiL$; all its object components are equivalences by Step 4. On the left-hand full category, whiskering the counit gives $G\mapsto G\epsilon:GLi\to G$, an equivalence by Step 2. Both are natural transformations of the two precomposition composites, not merely choices of equivalences on their objects: composing a coherent parameter simplex of functors with the fixed unit or counit supplies that simplex of transformations, compatibly with its faces and degeneracies. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore makes them natural equivalences. They exhibit the two precomposition functors as inverse equivalences of full coherent functor categories, hence identify natural transformations and all higher simplices. If $H:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$ is cocontinuous, postcomposition preserves the two full categories and carries the comparisons to $(HF)\eta$ and $(HG)\epsilon$ by associativity of composition. This is the asserted naturality in the target. All shapes used were small in the fixed universe; no colimit over the object collection of $\mathcal A$ or $\mathcal E$ was taken.

title: Cocontinuous functors factor through a small reflective localization
statement:
Use the universe and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and the mapping-space adjunctions of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints]. Let $\mathcal A$ be presentable, $S$ a small set of its arrows, and $L:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal A_S:i$ the reflective localization onto the objects $Z$ such that $\operatorname{Map}(s,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $s\in S$. Let $\mathcal E$ be any locally small infinity category admitting all small colimits, with no presentability hypothesis. Precomposition with $L$ induces an equivalence
$$L^*:\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(\mathcal A_S,\mathcal E)\simeq\{F\in\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{colim}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal E):F(S)\subseteq\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal E)\},$$
where both sides are full coherent functor categories. An inverse sends $F$ to $Fi$, which preserves small colimits. If $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to iL$ and $\epsilon:Li\to\mathrm{id}$ are the unit and counit, then $F\eta:F\to FiL$ and $G\epsilon:GLi\to G$ are the comparison equivalences. These give the displayed equivalence on natural transformations and all higher simplices, naturally in cocontinuous functors of $\mathcal E$.
